handback.t:
MESH-THINKER (X2) final report

## Head of Research verdicts (research_board.md line 84)
- **H1 SecondOpinion gate: VERIFIED CONDITIONALLY.** HoR's rerun matched mine exactly. The gate is net positive at c=0.05 in v-fixed and v-random. It loses where checkers are weak or useless and in v-notraps. HoR also flagged that I built the verification world myself. It stays opt-in, not default, and only makes sense for deployments that have real verifiers.
- **H3 ContextBench: REJECTED.** It did not beat the best baseline and I did not submit it.

## What I tested
I worked on two hypotheses:
- **H1: uncertainty-triggered second opinion.** This is `variants::SecondOpinion`, opt-in.
  - It ships no-harm by default: it uses no rng and the router gets the same feedback (the leader's outcome only), so the wrapped router (warm(hebbian-robust)) makes identical picks.
  - So success can only go up, through caught failures. The real test is net value: E-success minus c times E-calls.
  - It checks a leader's output only when P(leader fails) × q(checker) × P(retry succeeds) is greater than c × (1 + P(flag)).
  - It learns per feature × agent success, per feature × checker catch and false-alarm rates, and pools checker estimates across features.
- **H3: context-specific benching.** This is `mesh::ContextBenchConfig`, opt-in: per feature × agent health, with probation.
- I skipped H2 (calibration-based disagreement routing) as least promising.

**Verification world.** Built in x2_lab on top of `sim::World`, which I only read:
- A checker catches a failed output with probability q = qscale × skill and false-alarms with probability fascale × (1 − skill).
- Flags are verifiable: a flag triggers a retry by the best other agent.
- The "none" worlds (qscale 0, checks useless) stand in for the standard sim and serve as the no-harm test.

**Context world.** For H3: during a 30% window, one agent that is best on at least two types fails always on one of those types.

**Protocol.** Tuned on seeds 1–8, held-out seeds 31–60, paired 95% t-CI. Holm over the 34 main tests against the best of {keyword, eps-greedy, pooled-ts, hebbian-robust, warm(hebR), mesh-robust}; the ablations were Holm-corrected as a separate family. Two runs gave identical output.

## H1 held-out results
Differences are the gate's net value minus the best baseline's, at that cost.

| world | best baseline | net@0.05 (calls/task) | net@0.10 (calls/task) |
|---|---|---|---|
| v-fixed | warm(hebR) | **+0.0120** [+.0091,+.0149], 30/30 wins, BEATS (1.751) | **+0.0049** [+.0032,+.0066], 27/30, BEATS (1.170) |
| v-random | warm(hebR) | **+0.0111** [+.0074,+.0148], 28/30, BEATS (1.608) | **+0.0042** [+.0021,+.0063], Holm p=.0065, BEATS (1.130) |
| v-notraps | keyword | −0.0052, n.s. (1.639) | −0.0108, WORSE (1.124) |
| v-weak checkers | warm(hebR) | +0.0008, n.s. (1.222) | −0.0010, WORSE (1.030) |
| none-fixed | warm(hebR) | −0.0019, WORSE (1.038) | −0.0012, WORSE (1.012) |
| none-random | warm(hebR) | −0.0020, WORSE (1.040) | −0.0012, WORSE (1.012) |

- In v-fixed at c=0.05, E-success is 0.817 against 0.767 for warm(hebR).
- Ablations (Holm within that family): the gate beats always-check by +0.011 to +0.100 net in every world, and beats rate-matched random checking by +0.002 to +0.016 in every world with useful checkers. So the value comes from deciding when to doubt, not from checking itself.
- It is only modestly good at picking the right checker: the best checker is chosen in about 31–35% of checks, against 20% by chance.
- Pooling checker estimates across features cut the no-harm cost from about −0.007 to about −0.002.

## H3 held-out results
Against the best baseline, every world was n.s. (|diff| ≤ 0.003; ctx-fixed −0.0026/−0.0014, ctx-random +0.0006/+0.0012).
- Against mesh-robust it helps: +0.020 overall in ctx-random and +0.024 in ctx-notraps, both Holm-significant.
- But tuning picked a warm(hebR) leader, so that gain is mostly the leader, not the context benching.
